114.title: Primary straight-line AGM and runtime bounds

description: The logical route from the deployed verifier to the formal soundness endpoint.

stages.title: Pin Lean to the deployed verifier
stages.claim: The Lean assembler and a captured Rust verifier MSM agree coefficient-for-coefficient on the checked fixture.
stages.summary: The proof starts by fixing the object under study: the verifier's final multi-scalar multiplication. MsmMatch transfers a checked coefficient match to equality of group evaluations, but the deployed evidence remains fixture-based rather than a universal Rust-to-Lean equivalence.
proves: The checked Lean and captured Rust MSM coefficients match.
A matching MSM has the same group evaluation under any supplied URS.
residuals: Rust capture provenance and opaque-tag to Vesta-point faithfulness.
Deriving the deployed verifying key and circuit description inside Lean.

stages.title: Turn acceptance into the IPA equation
stages.claim: An accepting assembled MSM yields halo2's explicit IPA verifier equation.
stages.summary: DeployedAccepts is the concrete MSM-equals-identity premiss. deployedAccepts_verifierEq unfolds that compact check into the equation consumed by the soundness argument while retaining the verifier's rejection guards.
proves: The compact deployed accept implies the explicit verifier equation.
The soundness development now reasons about the equation actually assembled by the verifier.
residuals: The empirical verifier-fingerprint boundary from the preceding stage.
Fiat-Shamir challenges still need an oracle/rewinding interpretation.

stages.title: Rewind the oracle and assemble a tree
stages.claim: Enough accepting reprogrammed runs produce three distinct nonzero accepting continuations at every IPA round.
stages.summary: Transcript-ordering lemmas seal each round prefix before its challenge. The verifier equation becomes a concrete prover-strategy predicate, the counting forking lemma produces the branching executions, and deployed_forking_tree assembles them into the transcript tree used by special soundness.
proves: Round messages precede the challenges they must not influence.
The probability threshold yields the full accepting tree required by extraction.
residuals: Blake2b and challenge decoding are idealized as a uniform random oracle.
This #24 tree theorem is a consumer; the computed adversary, query-loss, and certificate producer are composed in the AGM stage.

stages.title: Peel the auxiliary generators
stages.claim: The deployed tree reduces to either a clean g-only IPA tree or a nontrivial relation over (g, U, W).
stages.summary: The deployed equation carries the U and W terms used for values and blinding. deployed_to_acceptV removes them when z is nonzero. Failure to separate them is exposed explicitly as the relation branch rather than hidden behind a binding axiom.
proves: The auxiliary-generator terms are removed on the clean branch.
Binding failure is retained as an explicit relation on the deployed augmented basis.
residuals: The legacy propositional capstones retain z != 0 and other rung-specific structural premisses.
The relation branch needs a computational reduction, not a propositional impossibility claim.

stages.title: Extract the IPA opening
stages.claim: A clean ternary transcript tree determines one witness that opens the commitment at the claimed inner product.
stages.summary: ipa_soundV applies three-special-soundness recursively. Distinct nonzero challenges make the Vandermonde reconstruction invertible, producing one coefficient vector shared by the commitment and value equations.
proves: The extracted vector commits to the verifier's pinned commitment.
The same vector has the extracted inner product value.
residuals: ipa_soundV consumes a completed tree; the deployed FS path constructs that tree in the AGM stage.
The alternative relation branch remains computationally meaningful.

stages.title: Price the relation branch
stages.claim: For represented online algebraic adversaries, with Fiat–Shamir challenges modelled as a random oracle, every explicit relation is reduced to discrete log with separately accounted oracle-query, Vesta group-work, and statistical terms.
stages.summary: The programmed-basis reduction plants the challenge in every basis slot and loses only one 1/|F| hyperplane. The adaptive-statement route erases its cost instrumentation back to the original game and reuses one cached execution for relation finding and witness extraction. Its quoted powers are resource coverage for a probability bound, not a universal security ceiling. The earlier recursive finder remains visible only in the pinned historical stages; #142 removed it from the live reduction stack.
proves: Every group point in the adaptive Fiat-Shamir adversary's proof output carries its representation over (g,U,W).
The pinned historical stack records how the retired recursive extractor computed an AlgebraicDForkCert; the live reduction no longer imports that route.
Every binding mismatch yields explicit relation data, and the programmed-basis conversion loses only one 1/|F| miss hyperplane.

The adaptive-statement finder and witness extractor reuse one adversary output, annotation log, and challenge vectors; the cached finder is pointwise equal to the original finder and extraction succeeds on exactly the same oracle tables.

The Action knowledge extractors are executable and return the actual private witnesses for every proof in the bundle together with proofs that they satisfy the compiled Action specification; both the adaptive-statement and straight-line/sequential relation projections share their route's data-bearing outcome.

The resource model keeps random-oracle queries, Vesta group operations, and direct-coordinate work separate. The DLOG advantage term is the conclusion of the programmed-basis reduction; the theorem does not take a DLOG-hardness proposition as a premiss.

For every Action count at or below Orchard's consensus maximum, the conditionally staged-certified adaptive-statement endpoints bound verifier acceptance with failed executable witness extraction by Adv_DLOG(2^124,2^126) + 2^-83. They cover represented online-AGM adversaries with random-oracle challenge derivation. At the separate Q ≤ 2^123 oracle parameter, both 2^123 and 2^125 adversary group-work budgets are covered; the latter's adversary-plus-reduction group work is at most 2^126. One closed program constructs the charged basis, specializes the exact adversary path with its annotations and group nodes, builds a proof-carrying cache, and feeds that same cache through reified verifier postprocessing. Lean proves its counter decomposition. Because the embedding is shallow, staging fidelity remains explicit for both the supplied adversary and generic host callbacks in the complete program. The three-decode bound follows from a required family representation-length invariant, not a concrete deployment family constructed here; the executable read-set bound also remains separate from the DLOG group budget.
residuals: Identify Blake2b and halo2's concrete hash-to-curve with their modeled random oracles, relate a concrete implementation to the costed algebraic program, choose a concrete interpretation of the resulting finite-resource Vesta DLOG advantage, and identify the extracted circuit witnesses with the ledger-level Orchard witness relation. The theorem covers represented online-AGM adversaries, not arbitrary non-algebraic random-oracle adversaries.

stages.title: Recover the verifier's opened columns
stages.claim: Rewinding x4 recovers the point-set aggregates; rewinding x1 binds those aggregates to the queried member commitments.
stages.summary: The x4 rewind floor produces a transfer from the pinned IPA opening to the power-batched openings consumed by the Vandermonde decode. The x1 layer then exposes the individual advice, instance, fixed, permutation, lookup, and vanishing commitments inside each aggregate.
proves: The x4 decode yields the deployed point-set aggregates, not modeled stand-ins.
The x1 unbatch pins the extracted witness to the actual queried member commitments.
residuals: The x4 accept-measure premiss and an accepting current run remain explicit.
Per-point claimed evaluations and x-to-x3 quotient transport remain in hquot.

stages.title: Lift the point check to circuit satisfaction
stages.claim: Outside the Schwartz-Zippel bad set, the quotient point check implies the full combined gate identity.
stages.summary: The bad-set theorem bounds roots of the constraint-difference polynomial. The xgood capstones spend an accept-measure budget to select a good accepting challenge, removing hgood while keeping the actual quotient-check content in hquot.
proves: A good challenge turns the verifier's point identity into the full gate polynomial identity.
The xgood family derives bad-set avoidance from an explicit probability budget.
residuals: hquot still carries the fingerprint-to-gate-check and x-to-x3 transport content.
Permutation/lookup grand-product telescoping and final lookup assembly are not wired into this relation.

stages.title: Compose legacy opening and circuit satisfaction
stages.claim: Given the accepting rewind data and structural premisses named by a legacy Vesta rung, Lean constructs one SnarkRelation joining the extracted IPA opening to circuit satisfaction for the same witness.
stages.summary: These are conditional extraction theorems over explicit transcript trees or accepting rewinds, not finite-resource guarantees for an executable adversary. They cover the abstract, deployed, adaptive, xgood, and x4 variants without assigning a numerical query or work envelope. The live represented-adversary probability guarantees and their coverage parameters are stated separately in the AGM stage.
proves: The legacy opening and constraint branches refer to the same pinned verifier statement.
Each legacy rung exposes the accepting execution data and structural conditions it requires.
residuals: These rungs do not by themselves model or resource-bound an executable adversary; different variants retain different structural and probability premisses.
SnarkRelation is not yet the intended high-level Ironwood security statement.

stages.title: Stop at the exact formal boundary
stages.claim: The formal chain reaches executable Action witnesses or explicit relation data and states every remaining model boundary as a premiss or documented interpretation step.
stages.summary: The strongest adaptive capstones cover represented online algebraic adversaries in the random-oracle model at explicit query and group-work parameters. Exact reduction data flow and counter composition are derived. The shallow cost language leaves explicit fidelity obligations for the supplied adversary and for generic host callbacks in the complete program; the direct-decode derivation depends on a required family length invariant. Legacy rewind rungs remain conditional on supplied accepting trees. Neither route identifies concrete hashes, the captured verifier artifact, or the compiled circuit witness with the ledger-level Orchard relation inside Lean.
proves: Every mechanized bridge shown in the map has a concrete Lean anchor.
The endpoint records reduction outcomes and residual premisses without hiding them.
residuals: High-level relation, VK derivation, Rust-capture trust, Blake2b-as-RO, generator hash-to-curve-as-RO, the AGM idealization, and a concrete interpretation of the finite-resource DLOG advantage.

The adaptive group-work result remains conditional on external adversary fidelity and on no hidden Vesta work in generic host callbacks of the complete shallow program. Exact reduction composition is derived; direct-decode coverage follows once the family supplies its required representation-length invariant. The legacy rewind capstones still require their named execution and probability premisses.
